title: The scoped ledger row read keeps a row with a quoted field holding a quote and matches a key in the last column
goal: kbfacts._ledger_rows returns the same rows as a full csv read for every cited id, including a row whose quoted field holds a doubled quote mid-field and a ledger whose key column is the last column; pack_freshness_stamp's test plants both cases, with no new test id

run:
import sys, csv, os, tempfile; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import kbfacts
q=chr(34); nl=chr(10)
p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'l.csv')
rows=['a,note,id', 'x,5'+q+' pipe,S1', 'y,'+q+'say '+q+q+'x'+q+q+' then, more'+q+',S2', 'z,plain,S3', 'w,'+q+'multi'+nl+'line '+q+q+'q'+q+q+q+',S4']
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(nl.join(rows)+nl)
full=list(csv.DictReader(open(p,encoding='utf-8',newline='')))
bad=[s for s in ('S1','S2','S3','S4') if kbfacts._ledger_rows(p,'id',{s})!=[r for r in full if r['id']==s]]
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

gates.question: How does the scoped ledger read find where a csv record ends and match its key without a full parse? Quote-state scan: follows csv's rule that a quote opens a field only at its start, reads the key of a plain record with its line ending stripped, shapes rows as csv.DictReader does, and keeps the no-parse path for rows of unwanted sources. Parity count: keeps the odd-quote join, which a bare quote mid-field breaks. Parse every quoted record: right but costs the parses the scan exists to avoid.
options: parity count with the key's line ending stripped

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 3 of 15, "Freshness at lookup: revalidation counts, memos, ledger reads and status agree"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Premise run 2026-10-13: a planted ledger (key in the last column; a row with a bare quote mid-field; a quoted field with a doubled quote; a quoted newline) read by _ledger_rows differs from a full csv read on the base for the last-column key and the bare quote (exit 1, checks index 1). The -k pack_freshness_stamp check (index 0) passes before the work because it pins the stamp behaviour that must stay and does not plant the cases yet; the worker plants them in that test, with no new test id.
